segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר פֵּירוֹת לַחֲבֵירוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו רוֹבַע טִנּוֹפֶת לִסְאָה. תְּאֵנִים – מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֶשֶׂר מְתוּלָּעוֹת לְמֵאָה. מַרְתֵּף שֶׁל יַיִן – מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֶשֶׂר קוֹסְסוֹת לְמֵאָה. קַנְקַנִּים בַּשָּׁרוֹן – מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֶשֶׂר פִּיטָסוֹת לְמֵאָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» When selling a significant quantity of produce or a number of items, there is a possibility that there will be a certain proportion of impurities in it or that some of the product will be of substandard quality. The mishna delineates what proportion is considered acceptable, for which a buyer may not demand compensation. With regard to «one who sells produce,» i.e., grain, «to another, this» buyer «accepts upon himself» that up to «a quarter-»kav of «impurities» may be present «in» each «se’a» of produce purchased. When purchasing «figs, he accepts upon himself» that up to «ten infested» figs may be present «in» each «hundred» figs purchased. When purchasing «a cellar» containing barrels «of wine, he accepts upon himself» that up to «ten» barrels of «souring» wine may be present «in» each «hundred» barrels purchased. When purchasing «jugs» of wine «in the Sharon» region, «he accepts upon himself» that up to «ten inferior-quality jugs [pitasot]» of wine may be present «in» each «hundred» jugs purchased.

moves.cueHe: המוכר פירות לחבירו, הרי זה מקבל עליו רובע טינופת לסאה
moves.summary: sets acceptable defect ratios in sales

positions.claim: a buyer accepts a quarter-kav of refuse per se'a of produce, and ten defective per hundred figs, wine barrels, or Sharon jugs
